title: Mastermind Arcade – Seeded, Scored, and Replayed

endpoints.response: { id: string; seed: number; guesses: { turn: number; code: number[]; black: number; white: number }[] }
{ id: string; turn: number; code: number[]; black: number; white: number }

sessions.title: Seeded game + board UI
sessions.goal: Persist games and guesses with Prisma, render the board, and submit guesses (feedback comes in session 2).

criteria.check: POST /api/games returns 201 with a JSON object containing id and seed
GET /api/games/[id] returns 200 with guesses as an empty array for a fresh game
Screen sc-board accepts four colour picks and Submit then shows one new guess row with four coloured pegs
POST /api/games/[id]/guesses with a 4-number code returns 201 with a JSON object echoing that code and a turn number

cuts.hint: Write the four currently selected colour ids into `payload` as { code: [d0,d1,d2,d3] } in slot order so the body you POST holds exactly those four numbers.
Create the Guess for this game by writing the posted 4-number code into `created` with the next turn number, then let the handler answer 201 with it.

sessions.title: Scoring and feedback pegs
sessions.goal: Score guesses deterministically and show black/white pegs per row.

criteria.check: Submitting the exact secret yields black=4 and white=0 on the last row in GET /api/games/[id]
After submitting a rotation of the secret (no positions match), GET /api/games/[id] returns 200 and the last guess shows black=0 and white=4

When the secret has repeats, after submitting a suitable guess, GET /api/games/[id] returns 200 and the last guess shows black+white equal to the count of matching colours after removing exact matches (no white double-counting)
Screen sc-board renders the exact number of black and white pegs per row based on stored black and white
After two submissions, sc-board renders two rows (one per guess)

cuts.hint: Set `black` to the count of positions i in 0..3 where secret[i] equals guess[i].
Set `white` to the count of colour-only matches after removing all exact matches so no colour is counted twice.
Build `feedback` for the visible row with exactly the stored `black` black pegs and `white` white pegs.
Map the game’s stored guesses into `rows` with one entry per guess in most-recent-first order and keep the four colours for each row.

sessions.title: Deterministic hint and remaining count
sessions.goal: Filter the 6^4 code space against the history and suggest the next guess deterministically.

criteria.check: GET /api/games/[id]/hint with no guesses returns 200 with remaining = 1296
After submitting [0,0,0,0] that scores 0 blacks and 0 whites, GET /api/games/[id]/hint returns remaining = 625
Screen sc-board shows "Hint: 1 1 1 1 • Remaining 625" after that zero-score first guess

cuts.hint: Fill `out` with every 4-long code from 0..5 whose score against each past guess equals that guess’s recorded black and white.
Put the first code in lexicographic ascending order from `candidates` into `out`, or null when no candidates remain.
Write the next hint code and remaining count into `hintText` as "Hint: d0 d1 d2 d3 • Remaining N".

sessions.title: Replay, resume, and branch
sessions.goal: List saved games, resume play, scrub through a game’s history, and branch a new line of play from any earlier turn.

criteria.check: GET /api/games returns 200 with an array of entries that include id, seed, guessCount, and status
Screen sc-games renders one row per saved game with its id, seed and guessCount; clicking a row resumes that game at /game/[id]
On sc-board, moving the Turn control to K shows exactly K guess rows from the start of the game
On sc-board, "Branch from turn K" creates a new game with the same seed and replays the first K guesses into it; after navigation the board shows exactly K rows

cuts.hint: Set `shownGuesses` to the first `step` guesses from the game’s history in order of play.
Populate `batch` with the codes of the first `step` guesses so the UI can POST them to the new game in order.
Produce one `rows` entry per saved game with its id, seed, and guessCount; newest first.
